figure.alt: Scatter plot for the 54 columns of the Great Isaiah Scroll. The x axis is column number; the y axis is the column number of each column's nearest neighbour in handwriting features. Early columns mostly have nearest neighbours in the low-to-mid 20s, later columns mostly in the 30s, and a fitted logistic curve steps up between about columns 25 and 30.
figure.credit: Fig 10 from Popović, Dhali & Schomaker (2021), PLOS ONE 16(4): e0249769, CC BY 4.0. Resized and converted to WebP.

figure.alt: Chart with one row per manuscript, from 4Q70 at the bottom to 5/6Hev1b at the top, on a time axis from about 300 BCE to 200 CE. Each row has coloured bars: blue for radiocarbon ranges, green for the Enoch model, red for traditional palaeographic estimates, black for a historical date. Labels on the right give each manuscript's script type: Archaic, Hasmonean, Herodian or Historical.
figure.credit: Fig 1 from Popović et al. (2025), PLOS ONE 20(6): e0323185, CC BY 4.0. Resized and converted to WebP.

figure.alt: Diagram of the 54 columns of 1QIsaa in a row. Columns 1 to 27 are tan, 28 to 54 green. A dashed line marks the seam between 27 and 28, column 27 is drawn shorter for the gap at its foot, and a bracket over 27 to 29 marks the handwriting switch found in 2021.
figure.credit: Our own diagram, drawn from the numbers in Popović, Dhali & Schomaker (2021). Not to scale.
